methods.label: Express 12 using the given bases
methods.explanation:
Since \(P\) and \(Q\) use bases \(2\) and \(3\), factor \(12\) as \(2^2\cdot3\). The power rules then give
\[
\begin{aligned}
12^{mn}
&=2^{2mn}3^{mn}\\
&=(2^m)^{2n}(3^n)^m\\
&=P^{2n}Q^m.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every base here is positive. Zero exponents give \(1\), and negative exponents mean reciprocals of nonzero quantities, so these steps remain valid for every pair of integers \((m,n)\).

The answer is \(P^{2n}Q^m\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
